key_insight: The paper tackles RGBT tracking when one modality is missing by using a conditional denoising transformer that can work with both complete and incomplete inputs. The core idea is to make tracking robust to missing thermal or RGB information without relying on fragile modality reconstruction.
problem_solved: Existing RGBT trackers often break down when one modality is absent or degraded, because they depend on reconstructing missing data from the other modality. This creates unstable features and poor performance in challenging real-world scenes, while also limiting flexibility for handling both full and partial modality inputs.
method: Introduces a spatio-temporal conditional denoising transformer for modality-missing RGBT tracking.
Uses conditional denoising to fuse available modalities and suppress noise caused by missing or incomplete inputs.
Designed to handle both complete and missing-modality scenarios more flexibly than methods that only focus on modality recovery.
impact: This approach can improve the robustness of multimodal tracking systems in real-world settings where sensors may fail or be partially unavailable. For practitioners, it offers a more reliable way to build trackers that gracefully degrade under missing data instead of collapsing.
visual_elements: A two-branch RGB + thermal tracking pipeline showing complete vs. missing modality cases.
A transformer block diagram highlighting spatio-temporal fusion and conditional denoising.
Before/after comparison of noisy missing-modality features versus cleaned robust features.
A performance chart comparing the proposed method with reconstruction-based baselines under modality dropout.
paper_title: Spatio-Temporal Conditional Denoising Transformer for Modality-Missing RGBT Tracking
paper_authors: Andong Lu, Ziyi Zha, Jiandong Jin, Shihao Li, Chenglong Li
